newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end on firm note after seesaw day.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end on firm note after seesaw day.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended Wednesday on a firm note -- although well off the day's highs-- after rotational trade in blue chip shares, brokers said.

Brokers said investors took the opportunity to do some portfolio re-positioning, selling underperformers and outperformers now that interest rate uncertainty had been eased by the U.S. decision on Tuesday to hold rates steady.
"It was a bit of a seesaw battle today," said James Robertson, institutional sales manager at Salomon Brothers.
The Hang Seng Index rose 56.83 points to 11,603.53, ending well off a late morning high of 11,653.36.
Turnover was respectable at HK$5.43 billion, in line with Tuesday's HK$10.8 billion which was inflated by two large share placements worth more than HK$5.0 billion.

The U.S. Federal Reserve's decision not to raise lending rates took the market by surprise. After an initial mark down of 34 points, the index rose 107 points to trade at the day's high of 11,653 before profit-taking and portfolio switching erased some of those gains.

Brokers said the market was split between those who saw the Fed's decision merely as delaying an inevitable rate increase, and those who saw it as confirmation that the US economy and inflationary forces had quieted for the near to medium term.
"I'm cautiously optimistic," said Priscilla Ng, executive director, at CEF GC Brokerage Ltd. "The trend suggests that there will be no need to raise U.S. interest rates in November either."
The property sector led the market, gaining 0.78 percent compared with the Hang Seng's 0.48 percent. The commercial and industrial sector followed with a rise of 0.71 percent.
In the property sector, Cheung Kong which has lagged market leaders, rose HK$1.00 to HK$56.70 on good turnover of HK$142.2 million
Among the conglomerates, Shun Tak jumped HK$0.55, or 10.8 percent, to HK$5.10. Brokers said buyers were looking for improved earnings from the company's share of a residential development.
CITIC Pacific held onto its HK$0.30 to end at HK$34.60 after trading at an intra-day high of HK$34.60, while Swire Pacific ended down HK$0.25 at HK$67.75.
HSBC shed HK$0.50 to HK$141.00. The share came under profit-taking pressure in London on rumours of a downgrading of the stock by a large U.S. broker, brokers said.
